claims: Artemis II is NASA's first crewed mission to the Moon in over 50 years.
Artemis II took four astronauts on a 10-day mission around the Moon and safely back.
Artemis II splashed down on April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II crew tested the Orion spacecraft's systems in deep space.
NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen flew around the Moon, reaching the far side.
The Artemis II crew set a new record for the farthest distance traveled from Earth by humans, reaching 252,756 miles (406,771 km) on April 6, 2026.
Victor Glover became the first person of color to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
Christina Koch became the first woman to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
Jeremy Hansen became the first non-U.S. citizen to travel beyond low Earth orbit.
The Artemis II astronauts performed manual flying tests.
The Artemis II astronauts evaluated life support systems.
The Artemis II astronauts tested the spacecraft's communication systems.
The Artemis II astronauts tested the new, improved toilet system.
The Artemis II crew observed the Moon’s surface, taking photos and notes to help determine geological composition.
Artemis II concluded with a successful splashdown in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California after a high-speed, high-temperature reentry.
